# Module map

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py -- do not edit by hand. Run `./docsis docs` to regenerate. -->

What lives where, from the package's own docstrings. The one structural rule worth stating: the CMTS and the cable modems hold no reference to each other. Everything between them goes through `phy.plant`, which is what keeps the simulation honest -- if a modem gets online, it did so by exchanging real DOCSIS frames.

## `docsislab`

### `docsislab/__main__.py`

docsislab command line.

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cmd_docs` | function | Regenerate docs/REFERENCE.md, CLI.md, API.md and docs/README.md. |

Also: `cmd_up`, `banner`, `report`, `cmd_run`, `cmd_cli`, `cmd_dash`, `cmd_cfg`, `find_tshark`, `cmd_pcap`, `cmd_scenarios`, `cmd_doctor`, `build_parser`, `main`.

## `docsislab.docsis`

The protocol itself: framing, messages, the configuration file, and the constants.

### `docsislab/docsis/cfgfile.py`

The DOCSIS configuration file: encode, decode, and the two MICs.

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cm_mic` | function | MD5 over the encoded settings, in file order, minus the MIC settings. |
| `cmts_mic` | function | MD5 over an ordered subset of the settings plus the shared secret. |
| `encode` | function | Serialise a config file, appending both MICs and the end marker. |
| `decode` | function | Parse a configuration file into settings, expanding compound TLVs. |
| `Verification` | class | The result of checking a configuration file's two MICs. |
| `verify` | function | Check both MICs over a decoded settings list (from a file or REG-REQ). |
| `build` | function | Compile a readable dict into configuration setting TLVs. |
| `modem_capabilities` | function | TLV 5, which the modem adds to REG-REQ (it is never in the config file). |
| `vendor_class_identifier` | function | DHCP option 60 as a DOCSIS modem sends it. |
| `dump` | function | Render config settings the way a config-file editor would show them. |

### `docsislab/docsis/consts.py`

DOCSIS 2.0 constants: frame control, message types, IUCs, TLVs, timers.

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FCType` | class | The two high bits of FC: which kind of frame this is. |
| `FCParm` | class | FC_PARM values when FC_TYPE == MAC_SPECIFIC. |
| `EHdrType` | class | Extended header element types -- RFIv2.0 Table 6-8. |
| `MgmtType` | class | MAC management message type codes (Table 6-15). |
| `IUC` | class | Interval Usage Codes: the kinds of upstream region a MAP allocates. |
| `UCDTLV` | class | Top-level TLVs inside an Upstream Channel Descriptor. |
| `BurstTLV` | class | Sub-TLVs inside a UCD burst descriptor (RFIv2.0 Table 8-3). |
| `Modulation` | class | UCD burst-descriptor modulation codes (RFIv2.0 Table 8-3). |
| `RngRspTLV` | class | TLVs inside a Ranging Response: the corrections the CMTS sends. |
| `RangingStatus` | class | What the CMTS thinks of a modem's ranging so far. |
| `RegRspCode` | class | Why the CMTS accepted or refused a registration. |
| `ConfirmationCode` | class | RFIv2.0 Annex C.4 -- also used by DSA/DSC. |
| `CfgTLV` | class | Configuration settings: the config file's contents, echoed in REG-REQ. |
| `ClassOfServiceTLV` | class | Sub-TLVs of CfgTLV.CLASS_OF_SERVICE (Annex C.1.1.4). |
| `CapTLV` | class | Sub-TLVs of CfgTLV.MODEM_CAPABILITIES (Annex C.1.3.1). |
| `UpstreamSymbolRate` | class | Bit positions in CapTLV.UPSTREAM_SYMBOL_RATES. |
| `DocsisVersion` | class | Spec revision a modem claims in its Modem Capabilities. |
| `SFTLV` | class | Service flow encodings, sub-TLVs of type 24/25 (Annex C.2.2). |
| `QoSParamSet` | class | Which QoS parameter sets a service flow encoding applies to. |
| `SchedulingType` | class | Upstream scheduling discipline for a service flow. |

### `docsislab/docsis/frames.py`

Putting a MAC management message on the wire, and taking it off again.

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mgmt_version` | function | The `version` byte a given message type must carry. |
| `encode_mgmt` | function | Encode a message object into a complete DOCSIS MAC frame. |
| `ParsedFrame` | class | A decoded MAC frame plus, where applicable, its decoded contents. |
| `parse` | function | Decode a MAC frame and, where applicable, its management message. |

### `docsislab/docsis/machdr.py`

The DOCSIS MAC frame header -- RFIv2.0 section 6.2.1.

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MacFrameError` | class | A MAC frame that cannot be encoded or decoded. |
| `EHdrElement` | class | One element inside the extended header. |
| `ehdr_request` | function | A piggybacked bandwidth request (EH_TYPE 1): request `minislots` for `sid`. |
| `encode_ehdr` | function | Serialise extended header elements into the EHDR field. |
| `MacFrame` | class | A decoded DOCSIS MAC frame. |
| `build_mgmt_frame` | function | Wrap an already-encoded MAC management message in a MAC header. |
| `build_packet_pdu` | function | Wrap an Ethernet frame (including its 4-byte FCS) as a Packet PDU. |
| `build_request` | function | A bandwidth Request frame: six bytes, no payload. |
| `build_concatenation` | function | Concatenation header (DOCSIS 1.1+): several MAC frames in one burst. |
| `decode` | function | Decode one MAC frame, verifying the HCS. |
| `decode_all` | function | Decode a concatenation body / burst containing several MAC frames. |

### `docsislab/docsis/messages.py`

Encoders and decoders for the DOCSIS 2.0 MAC management messages.

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MessageError` | class | A MAC management message body that cannot be parsed. |
| `Sync` | class | Downstream timestamp.  The CMTS latches its 32-bit 10.24 MHz master clock into this field; every modem on the downstream slaves its own clock to the arriving value, which is what makes upstream mini-slot timing possible in the first place. |
| `BurstDescriptor` | class | Per-IUC burst profile.  The IUC is the first byte of the descriptor value, followed by sub-TLVs.  A type-4 descriptor is DOCSIS 1.x; a type-5 descriptor is DOCSIS 2.0 and may carry the interleaver, preamble-type and S-CDMA parameters that 1.x has no way to express. |
| `Ucd` | class | Upstream Channel Descriptor. |
| `MapIE` | class | One 32-bit MAP information element: SID(14) \| IUC(4) \| offset(14). |
| `Map` | class | Upstream Bandwidth Allocation: who may transmit in which mini-slots. |
| `RngReq` | class | Ranging Request: SID 0 for initial ranging, the assigned SID after. |
| `RngRsp` | class | Ranging Response: timing, power and frequency corrections, plus status. |
| `RegReq` | class | Registration Request: the config file settings echoed back, plus capabilities. |
| `RegRsp` | class | Registration Response: accept or refuse, and the assigned SFIDs and SIDs. |
| `RegAck` | class | Registration Acknowledge: the modem confirms, and is then in service. |
| `UccReq` | class | Upstream Channel Change Request: move to another upstream. |
| `UccRsp` | class | Upstream Channel Change Response, sent on the channel being left. |
| `DsxReq` | class | DSA-REQ / DSC-REQ / DSD-REQ share a transaction-ID + TLV shape. |
| `DsxRsp` | class | DSA/DSC/DSD response and acknowledge: transaction ID plus a confirmation code. |
| `decode_body` | function | Decode a MAC management payload according to its type byte. |

## `docsislab.net`

Networking: packet encoding, the provisioning protocols, a small IP stack, and the macOS utun bridge.

### `docsislab/net/dhcp.py`

DHCP, as DOCSIS uses it.

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Dhcp` | class | A DHCP message, including the DOCSIS-relevant BOOTP fields. |

Also: `decode`, `discover`, `request`, `reply`.

### `docsislab/net/packet.py`

Minimal Ethernet / ARP / IPv4 / UDP / ICMP encoding.

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checksum16` | function | The one's-complement Internet checksum (RFC 1071). |
| `Ethernet` | class | An Ethernet II frame, padded to the 60-byte minimum on encode. |
| `Arp` | class | An ARP request or reply over Ethernet and IPv4. |
| `IPv4` | class | An IPv4 packet; the header checksum is computed on encode. |
| `UDP` | class | A UDP datagram; the checksum needs the IP addresses, so encode takes them. |
| `udp_datagram` | function | A complete IPv4 packet carrying UDP. |
| `ICMP` | class | An ICMP message, echo request and reply in practice. |
| `describe` | function | One line summarising an Ethernet frame, for logs and pcap comments. |

Also: `mac_str`, `mac_bytes`, `ip_str`, `ip_bytes`, `ip_int`, `in_subnet`, `decode_ethernet`, `decode_arp`, `decode_ipv4`, `decode_udp`, `decode_icmp`, `icmp_echo`.
